data.narrative:
The Lumber Manufactory is a Series C robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $53.1M to date. Valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 9 comparable companies (1 public, 8 private) operating in the same sector at similar or adjacent stages, including Exotec, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, and Hadrian.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total raised as a proxy baseline of $53M and applying a 1.7x multiplier typical for Series C advancement, implies a valuation of $90M. Peer-median analysis across 7 same-sector comparables yielded a median valuation of $1.6B, with a range spanning $1.0B to $2.0B. The sample includes Exotec ($2.0B, Series D), Hadrian ($1.6B, Series D), Dexterity ($1.6B, Series B), and Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B, Series B).

The two methods generate a wide implied range of $77M to $1.9B, with a median of $870M. The stage-progression method implies conservative valuation anchored to capital deployment; the peer-median method reflects current market multiples for robotics-sector companies at overlapping stages. Key uncertainties driving the wide dispersion include: revenue scale and profitability relative to peers, stage-to-stage execution risk, and whether peer valuations reflect sustainable market pricing or sector inflation. Additional operational metrics—revenue, customer concentration, gross margins—would be required to narrow the range meaningfully.
